title: ailocalpack anti-cheat policy
description: The anti-cheat policy: the list bundled with the app (src/AiLocalPack.Core/AntiCheat/anti-cheat.json) and the registry's policy/anti-cheat.json (maintainers only), in the same format. The app puts the registry's on top of the bundled one: a registry rule replaces the bundled rule with its id and new ones are added, a game listed in `games` takes that anti-cheat, the `allowed` lists add up. `ailocalpack index build` publishes the registry's rules in index.json (`antiCheats`) and the games as `antiCheat` / `antiCheatAllowed`. Games with an anti-cheat are blocked for install and generation unless allowed. A broken file stops the index build. Unknown properties are allowed (forward compatibility); a breaking change raises schemaVersion.

games.description: Games known to use an anti-cheat that leaves no files in the game folder (kernel anti-cheats installed elsewhere); each listed once. The anti-cheat is one of this file's or, in the registry's file, one of the app's bundled list.

allowed.description: Games that officially allow mods (whitelist): never blocked for an anti-cheat, found in the files or listed. An opt-out still blocks them.

note.description: For maintainers (not shown): a link to the studio's statement that mods are allowed.

antiCheatId.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; `none` is reserved (a game checked without a finding).

markers.description: Files or folders that show the anti-cheat, checked in every folder of the game tree (6 levels deep): a name (`BEClient_x64.dll`), a folder with a trailing '/' (`EasyAntiCheat/`) or a short path (`pb/pbcl.dll`); '*' and '?' only in the last part; names ignore case.
